The man who built one of the most valuable companies on Earth just lost his job.
And it may have started with a spy.
For thirty-three years, Jensen Huang ran Nvidia, the company whose chips power artificial intelligence.
Those chips are so powerful that America restricts selling them to China.
Then, in October, the New York Times reported something strange.
U.S. intelligence believed that a businesswoman, whose company bought Nvidia's chips, had been recruited by Chinese intelligence to get close to him.
China called it groundless. No one has been charged, and her exact role is still unclear.
But Huang reportedly admitted to an affair, and the board opened an investigation.
Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe any secrets were compromised.
